blocks.x: Data & Lakehouse applied to Capabilities. This page sets out the operating context, the delivery pattern we run, the services and platforms involved, and the outcomes we commit to.

In Energy & Utilities, data, analytics & lakehouse is the substrate tower: pipeline modernization, lakehouse architecture on databricks and snowflake, streaming and event-driven decisioning, executive bi, master data and cataloging, predictive analytics, and data products that generate revenue. That is the baseline pattern; the differentiator is what it connects to: data engineering & pipeline modernization, lakehouse architecture & migration, real-time streaming & event-driven decisioning — delivered on Dataq Forge and Dataq Nexus with the sector's regulatory posture built in.

items: Renewable supply and flexible demand make legacy forecasting blind; imbalance costs and curtailment climb while forecasts run on yesterday's methods.
Scope 1/2/3 reporting pulls from meter readings, invoices and estimates with no lineage; auditors begin to ask what accountants always ask: prove it.
IT/OT convergence, remote access growth and legacy SCADA estates create attack paths with physical consequences; CIP/NIS2 duties expand faster than programs mature.

blocks.x: How we deliver it in this sector

The delivery pattern composes 7 services from the Data, Analytics & Lakehouse tower — Data Engineering & Pipeline Modernization, Lakehouse Architecture & Migration, Real-Time Streaming & Event-Driven Decisioning, Enterprise BI & Executive Analytics as the usual core — sequenced through the Dataq Method with sector controls: REMIT / MiFID II obligations shape the design from the first sprint.
Services we deploy in this sector

items: Resilient, observable pipelines: trusted data from source to decision at SLA.
Lakehouse the right way: Unity Catalog governance, cost-aware design and AI-ready foundations.
Decisions at event speed: sub-second pipelines from sensor, click or transaction to action.
Metrics into management: one governed semantic layer, decision cadence built in.
SCADA/AMI/weather streams into one governed estate with lineage (forecasting and ops on the same truth)
Metered energy/emissions with lineage to disclosure reports (audit-ready reporting on schedule)
Unplanned outage hours on critical assets

blocks.x: Two regimes anchor the control design here: REMIT / MiFID II and NERC CIP (North America). Critical-infrastructure protection standards for bulk power systems. Evidence for both is generated by the delivery itself — control tests, replay trails and documentation are artifacts of the program, not a reconstruction project.

Delivery follows the same weekly rhythm on every program of this type. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
